partner_result_applied.use: Exact Choquet representation of each admissible marginal as a probability barycenter of measure-one indicator densities, inserted directly into the regularized interval inequality.

later_supporting_result_consumed.scope_used: Compatibility check only: the diffuse-range theorem permits arbitrary coordinate-separable phases, so the auxiliary epsilon Z^2 regularizer does not spoil its <27 branch when treated as a separable phase.

new_mathematical_result.statement: For every finite C, full QFORM with universal density constant C is equivalent, with exactly the same C, to the target-admissible family Q_epsilon=X^TAX+epsilon Z^2 for all 0<epsilon<1, where Z has fixed admissible triangular density rho(z)=(1-|z-2|)_+. Every Q_epsilon has a globally Lipschitz density. Using the partner Choquet theorem, one may simultaneously reduce the input laws to arbitrary measure-one indicator products without loss of C.

unresolved_implication: Prove a density/small-ball bound uniform in epsilon for X_E^T A X_E + epsilon Z^2 over the full three-large-eigenvalue matrix class and arbitrary measure-one indicator marginals. Original-output continuity remains separate.
next_step: Exploit the free pointwise/Lipschitz representative only in estimates whose constants can be kept independent of epsilon; combine with the regularized-determinant diffuse branch where applicable and attack the heavy-coordinate/nonseparable remainder without invalid conditional-cap or single-minor reductions.
